title: A Game Of Go At Lunch Gave The World QR Codes
description: One engineer was stuck for months until he sat down for a lunchtime game of Go. https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2020/dec/11/qr-code-inventor-relish-its-role-in-tackling-covid Would you have given it away for free? #anime #shorts #animestory #retroanime #truestory #history

characters.Masahiro Hara: 35-year-old Japanese engineer in 1992, short neat black hair parted on the side, clean shaven, white short-sleeve dress shirt with sleeves rolled, plain navy tie, gray slacks, black leather shoes, no hat, no glasses
characters.Teammate: 30-year-old Japanese engineer in 1992, short spiky black hair, light blue work shirt, dark gray work vest, khaki slacks, no hat
characters.Factory Worker: 28-year-old Japanese woman in 1992, black hair tied in a low ponytail, pale gray factory work jacket over a white shirt, navy work trousers, white cotton gloves, no hat
characters.Older Hara: Masahiro Hara at 63, short gray hair parted on the side, light wrinkles, charcoal cardigan over a white collared shirt, gray slacks, no hat, no glasses

scenes.say: There's a board game hiding on your phone, and it started on one man's lunch break. In 1992, Masahiro Hara was a quiet engineer at a car parts company in Japan.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Close-up of a wooden Go board with a few black and white stones on its grid lines, on a table inside a quiet 1990s Japanese factory break room. [4-7s] Medium shot: Masahiro Hara at his gray steel desk inside the Denso engineering office, fluorescent lights overhead, sleeves rolled up, looking tired. [7-10s] Masahiro Hara alone at his desk inside the Denso engineering office at dusk, orange light through the window, holding a cup of green tea.

scenes.say: But the factory floor was miserable. Each barcode held only about twenty characters, so workers scanned around a thousand of them a day, box after box, until their arms ached.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside a 1990s car parts warehouse, Factory Worker lifts a plain cardboard box marked only with small black striped stickers, no writing. [4-7s] Close-up of Factory Worker's gloved hand pressing a chunky gray handheld scanner against the box again and again, a red light flickering. [7-10s] Factory Worker rubs her sore shoulder between tall metal shelves of plain boxes inside the warehouse while Masahiro Hara watches from the end of the aisle.

scenes.say: So Hara and one teammate spent months trying to fit more information into one small label. Nothing worked. Then, one lunch break, he sat down to play Go.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Masahiro Hara and Teammate lean over a desk inside the Denso engineering office, crumpled blank graph paper piled everywhere. [4-7s] Close-up: Teammate shakes his head while Masahiro Hara rubs his eyes at the desk. [7-10s] Inside the quiet factory break room at noon, Masahiro Hara sits across a wooden Go board from Teammate, holding one white stone between two fingers.

scenes.say: He looked down at the board. Black and white stones sitting on a grid, and anyone can read where every stone is at a glance, even when one sits slightly crooked.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Close-up of Masahiro Hara's eyes slowly widening over the Go board inside the factory break room. [4-7s] Top-down shot of the wooden Go board in the factory break room: black and white stones scattered across the grid, a stripe of sunlight across it. [7-10s] Close-up of Masahiro Hara's finger nudging one crooked black stone off its line; he slowly smiles.

scenes.say: So he turned the barcode into a grid of black and white squares. It held two hundred times more, and still worked with almost a third of it smudged.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside the Denso engineering office, Masahiro Hara fills a grid of small black squares on blank graph paper with a pencil while Teammate leans in. [4-7s] Close-up: Teammate presses a coffee thumbprint onto a printed square of black and white blocks and holds the gray handheld scanner over it. [7-10s] The scanner light turns green; Masahiro Hara and Teammate grin at each other across the desk.

scenes.say: Denso released it in 1994 and let anyone use it for free. Hara doesn't earn a cent per scan. So every QR code on your phone is still his lunch break.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Medium shot: Older Hara sits at a wooden table inside a small quiet Tokyo cafe, sipping coffee by the window. [4-7s] Close-up of Older Hara's hand placing one white stone on a small travel Go board on the cafe table. [7-10s] Older Hara looks out the cafe window at soft evening rain and smiles quietly to himself.
